explanations.answer: The LORD's servant Moses had commanded it
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. Joshua built it "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). The text even says he built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses (Joshua 8:31). So this wasn't Joshua winging it like a man with no recipe. He was following the instructions he'd been given.

explanations.answer: The elders of Israel had asked for it
explanations.explanation: The elders are there, standing with all Israel in verse 33, but the text never says they asked for the altar. It says Joshua built it "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). The text also says he built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses (Joshua 8:31). Sometimes the people in the room aren't the people who gave the order.

explanations.answer: The Levitical priests had asked for it
explanations.explanation: The Levitical priests do show up in this passage, carrying the ark of the covenant (Joshua 8:33). But the text never says they asked for the altar. It points to Moses, the servant of the LORD, who had commanded it (Joshua 8:31). Good guess, though, because priests and altars do go together.

Uncut is right. The Book of the Law of Moses said, "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). Joshua built it according to what was written. Leaving things exactly as they are is hard for a stamper like me, but Joshua pulled it off.

Polished sounds fancy, but that's not what the Book said. It called for "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). The word you want is uncut. Joshua built it according to what was written.

Carved isn't what the Book said. It called for "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). So the word you want is uncut. I'm a stamper, so I totally get why carving sounds right to me.

True. Joshua 8:31 says, "…on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and they sacrificed peace offerings." Both kinds are named right there. The text says they built the altar according to what is written in the Book of the Law, and then they offered on it.

This one is true, so False misses it. The text says, "…on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and they sacrificed peace offerings." (Joshua 8:31). Both offerings are named right there. The altar didn't just sit on the mountain looking nice.

explanations.answer: A copy of the law of Moses
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Joshua "…inscribed on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written." (Joshua 8:32). He did it right there with all the Israelites watching. That's a lot of words to put on stones, so I hope he stretched his hand first.

explanations.answer: The names of the twelve tribes
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anything about tribe names on those stones. It says Joshua "…inscribed on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written." (Joshua 8:32). The words carved were the law itself. Tribe names would've been a much shorter job.

explanations.answer: A record of the battle at Ai
explanations.explanation: Ai had just fallen (Joshua 8:28), so I see why you'd go there. But the stones don't carry a battle report. Joshua "…inscribed on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written." (Joshua 8:32). The words on the stones were the law.

Look at verse 33 again. It says "All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike…" stood on both sides of the ark. So foreigners were in that crowd, which makes this statement False. There was room for everybody.

Right, the statement is False. Joshua 8:33 says, "All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" Foreigners and citizens alike were in that crowd. Everybody had a spot.

Bless it is! Moses had commanded it earlier, and the text states the purpose plainly: to bless the people of Israel (Joshua 8:33). Half stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, on both sides of the ark. That's a whole lot of standing for a good cause.

Counting a whole crowd that size would take forever, and I'd lose my place around the fortieth row. The text gives another purpose. They stood there "…as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel." (Joshua 8:33). The word you want is bless.

Judges were in that crowd, yes (Joshua 8:33). But the standing wasn't about judging anybody. The text says they stood there "…as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel." (Joshua 8:33). The word you want is bless.

Not quite. Joshua 8:34 says he "…read aloud all the words of the law—the blessings and the curses…" He read both. Skipping the hard parts is what I do with the terms and conditions, not what Joshua did.

That's right, the statement is False. The text says Joshua "…read aloud all the words of the law—the blessings and the curses—according to all that is written in the Book of the Law." (Joshua 8:34). Blessings and curses both got read. He didn't pick only the nice parts.

explanations.answer: The women and the little ones
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Joshua read "…before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them." (Joshua 8:35). The women and the little ones are named right there in the assembly. That's who else was listening.

explanations.answer: The kings of the nearby cities
explanations.explanation: Kings? That's a fancy guest list, friend! The passage doesn't name any kings among the listeners. It says Joshua read "…before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them." (Joshua 8:35). So the answer is the women and the little ones.

Ai is a fair thing to think of, since the city had just fallen (Joshua 8:28). But the text doesn't mention any captives at this reading. It says "…the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them." (Joshua 8:35). The answer is the women and the little ones.
